change.title: pr-33832-flat
change.description: Add AuthzClientCryptoProvider for authorization client cryptographic operations
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Multiple providers no longer fail fast; ties are resolved silently
findings.body: The old check threw when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath. Now the provider with the highest order() wins. Default, Elytron and FIPS all return 200, so if two of them end up on the classpath the winner depends on ServiceLoader order, and the only trace is a debug log. Give the three real providers distinct orders, or keep the exception when the top two orders are equal.

findings.title: Pre-built string passed as a format string
findings.body: logger.debugf(builder.toString()) uses the message as a format string. Class names rarely contain '%', but use debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", ...) or String.join instead. The trailing ", " is also left in the message.

findings.title: Dead statements in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: Lines 114-115 build ASN1Encoder objects and discard them. They have no effect, so remove them.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default keystore's provider
findings.body: The method returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which is the SUN provider and not BouncyCastle. Callers that expect BC from this method get a different provider. Consider throwing UnsupportedOperationException like the other unsupported methods, or document the behaviour.

findings.title: Malformed DER gives unchecked exceptions instead of IOException
findings.body: readLength returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding. readInteger then calls read(-1) and throws NegativeArraySizeException. In readSequence a negative length is never rejected. A sequence element that reads zero bytes would make the `length > 0` loop spin forever. The signature comes from the token or server input, so reject length < 0 with an IOException, and check that each element advances.

findings.title: Test uses one EC key size and does not init CryptoIntegration
findings.body: KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC") uses the default curve, which is P-256 on most JDKs. The ES384 and ES512 tests therefore sign with a P-256 key. Their signatures are 64 bytes but are decoded with signLength 96 and 132, so those cases only check that the round trip is stable and do not test real P-384 or P-521 signatures. Initialise the generator with secp384r1 and secp521r1 for those tests. The test also never calls AuthzClient.create or CryptoIntegration.init, so it does not cover the service-loader wiring.

summary: The change adds a minimal authz-client crypto provider with order-based selection. I found no blockers. The main concerns are that duplicate providers are now chosen silently and that the new ASN.1 decoder handles malformed DER poorly. The ES384/ES512 tests also use a P-256 key, so they don't exercise real P-384 or P-521 signatures. I did not trace the contracts, so that list is empty.
